Every triangle has exactly three Hessler.why: A made-up kind of point given to a real class (triangles). Absent from Dolma and from a web search.

sources.note: No triangle point of that name; hits were unrelated triangle-geometry papers and a list of triangle centres without it.

Every equilateral triangle is a triangle.why: By definition, first sentence of the Equilateral triangle article.

sources.quote: An equilateral triangle is a triangle with three sides of equal length and three equal angles.

A regular octahedron has eight faces, ea.why: Stated in the Octahedron article; one of the five Platonic solids.

sources.quote: One special case is the regular octahedron, a Platonic solid composed of eight equilateral triangles, four of which meet at each vertex.

notes: Fictional relation, TBox: a real class (triangles) with a made-up count. 'Exactly three' is a number restriction (dl). New member PQR in the prompt; the equilateral triangle is a well-known member, determinate here because it is a triangle by definition and holds no stored Hessler count (mathematics TBox, and the property is made up). d3 and d4 multiply (fol, arithmetic); d4 says 'counting each face separately' so shared points between faces don't make the total ambiguous.
